# Minimum Subsequence in Non-Increasing Order. Expected results list the
# kept values from largest to smallest.

@example The total is 22. 9 alone is less than the 13 left; 9 and 7 make 16, more than the 6 left.
[2,9,4,7]
=> [9,7]

@example 5 alone only ties the 3 and 2 left, so 3 is kept as well.
[5,3,2]
=> [5,3]

@example Two of the four 3s tie the other two; three of them are needed, and each is listed.
[3,3,3,3]
=> [3,3,3]

# One item: nothing is left over.
[42]
=> [42]

# Two equal items: one only ties the other.
[8,8]
=> [8,8]

# Two different items: the larger one wins.
[1,100]
=> [100]

# One item worth more than all the others together (10 against 9).
[3,1,10,2,3]
=> [10]

# One item worth exactly as much as all the others: one more is needed.
[3,1,9,2,3]
=> [9,3]

# An odd total, 9: 4 is less than half of it, though not less than 9 / 2
# rounded down.
[4,3,2]
=> [4,3]

# Already sorted from smallest to largest; the answer is listed the other way.
[1,2,3,4,5,6]
=> [6,5]

# All equal with an odd count: 3 of the 5.
[7,7,7,7,7]
=> [7,7,7]

# Two of the four 5s are needed, not all of them.
[5,9,5,5,1,5]
=> [9,5,5]

# The kept values repeat, apart in nums.
[2,8,3,8,1]
=> [8,8]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[3,2,2,3,2,3,2,21,3]
=> [21]

@gen 2 small
[5,3,3,1,1,1,5]
=> [5,5]

@gen 3 small
[2,3,3,12,3,2]
=> [12,3]

@gen 4 small
[1,1,3,2]
=> [3,2]

@gen 5 small
[2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]
=> [2,2,2,2,2,2]

@gen 8 small
[4,3,6,1,6,1,4]
=> [6,6,4]

@gen 10 small
[6,3,5,1,6,6,4,3]
=> [6,6,6]

@gen 13 small
[2,1,2,6,3]
=> [6,3]
